bug_semantics: The JAX-RS configuration endpoints (/api/configuration/{name} and /api/configuration/detailed/{name}) passed the path parameter into Configs.validate(), whose blacklist rejected literal slash, backslash, '..', blank input, and a trailing dot but allowed percent signs and other non-allowlisted characters. The validated name was then appended with '.cfg' and passed to ConfigUtil.getConfigStream(), which constructs and opens a filesystem path under the configured directory. At introduction the routes sat behind Jetty DigestAuthenticator on /* (only /api/health was unauthenticated). GHSA-hxf2-gm22-7vcm and published CVE-2026-35583 classify this as CWE-22 because encoded, double-encoded, or normalization variants could bypass the blacklist and disclose configuration data outside the intended directory.
flaw_origin: PR #352 introduced the configuration API and the vulnerable blacklist in squash commit 99ef64d4860d9a113c4c6482ef8e575330123f83. GitHub's surviving PR-member history decomposes that squash into 91a632b5fc860028b962d14ec163a387a45d2541, 70cdc725f0bf90e81871bd92a9864c95775b78ed, and c6f68a96ead85c57bfee5873a77ac72616708091. The first member, 91a632b5fc860028b962d14ec163a387a45d2541, adds Configs.java with the vulnerable validate() method; its parent 6443531b40f3a2c5096bf8a0f0419324a1385f84 lacks that file. The later members preserve validate(), so 91a632b5fc860028b962d14ec163a387a45d2541 is the atomic BIC.
